findings.note: Coward tied his season high with 23 points in 33 minutes on Nov. 14 while Ty Jerome (hip) and Zach Edey (ankle) were out, and he is shooting 43.5% from three. If either teammate is still out against Cleveland, his usage could stay high; no status for this game was found.

NBA.com lists Coward at 14.1 PPG, below the 15.5 line, as a starter. In his last five games he scored 18, 23, 14, 15 and 3 in 27 to 33 minutes, so he went over in each of his two most recent games and under in the three before that.

As of Nov. 12, Coward was averaging 12.8 points per game, and much of his value came from rebounds, threes and steals rather than heavy scoring. That supports a points total below 15.5, though he has scored more since then.
As of Nov 12, this RotoWire/CBS update had Coward averaging 2.3 made threes per game, which is above the 1.5 line; that came after he made 1 of 4 threes against Denver.

On Nov 14 he made 4 of 6 threes in 33 minutes while Ty Jerome (hip) and Zach Edey (ankle) were out. He is shooting 43.5% from three this season, up from 33.8% as a rookie, which suggests a bigger role, though that rate could fall back.

His last five games show 2, 4, 0, 1 and 1 made threes on 4 to 6 attempts each (Under 1.5 hit in 3 of 5), including 2 of 4 in 27 minutes at Washington on Nov 16. I found no injury report for Nov 18 or any analyst pick on this market.

ESPN's stats page shows Boozer averaging about 15.5 points and 5.2 assists, roughly 21 points plus assists, and 15.6 + 5.3 over his last 10 games, both well under 24.5; his road split (17.3 + 6.2) is closer to the line.

Contrary sign: in his last game, at Washington on 11/16, he had a career-high 29 points and 7 assists (36), and he had 22 points and 8 assists (30) at Toronto on 11/9; he has gone over 24.5 in 2 of his last 5 games and starts every game at about 31 minutes.

CBS lists Boozer at +290 for Rookie of the Year and shows him averaging 15.9 points and 5.5 assists; it found no injury or role concerns, and no Cavaliers injury, lineup or analyst pick for this market came up.

build.note: Ice time × production per 60 minutes, both recency-weighted and blended with a position average, then scaled by how many goals the opponent allows compared with the league. build.note: Ice time × production per 60 minutes, both recency-weighted and blended with a position average, then scaled by how many goals the opponent allows compared with the league. Then adjusted for how he has done against our own forecasts: 197 points against 173.1 forecast in his earlier games, shrunk toward no adjustment. The model then turns this average into the chance of each count.

player_context.note: Newer appearances carry more weight. Ice time has a 14-appearance half-life; production per minute has a 110-appearance half-life. The offseason does not age player history. Expected shots scale with the opponent’s shots allowed, and scoring with its goals allowed, relative to the league. A player who has consistently beaten (or missed) our earlier forecasts gets a shrunk adjustment toward that record. Observed averages below are unweighted. Participation and current role remain unconfirmed.
